es: Resolver un caso nuevo que reúne las cinco hebras del programa: antecedente personal, argumento con concesión, evaluación de una fuente, tacto ante otra postura y revisión documentada.

teaching.en: I would like to start with some background: years ago I used to be afraid of speaking English, and I would rehearse every sentence silently before I dared to say it aloud.
teaching.es: Me gustaría empezar con algunos antecedentes: hace años me daba miedo hablar inglés, y ensayaba cada frase en silencio antes de atreverme a decirla en voz alta.
teaching.explanationEs: Used to y would sitúan hábitos pasados; el pasado simple marca el cambio posterior.
segments: I would like to start with some background: years ago I used to be afraid of
speaking English, and I would rehearse every sentence silently before I dared to say it aloud.
teaching.audioText: I would like to start with some background: years ago I used to be afraid of speaking English, and I would rehearse every sentence silently before I dared to say it aloud.

teaching.en: In hindsight, the long journey mattered more than any single day, and it is not enough to reach a milestone if the habits behind it disappear.
teaching.es: Visto en retrospectiva, el largo recorrido importó más que cualquier día concreto, y no basta con alcanzar un hito si los hábitos que lo hicieron posible desaparecen.
teaching.explanationEs: La retrospectiva da perspectiva a un relato personal y conecta el pasado con el presente.
segments: In hindsight, the long journey mattered more than any single day, and it
is not enough to reach a milestone if the habits behind it disappear.
teaching.audioText: In hindsight, the long journey mattered more than any single day, and it is not enough to reach a milestone if the habits behind it disappear.

teaching.en: Before relying on a source, a critical reader asks who wrote it and what data it offers, because a source with no author and no evidence has little credibility.
teaching.es: Antes de fiarse de una fuente, un lector crítico pregunta quién la escribió y qué datos ofrece, porque una fuente sin autor y sin evidencia tiene poca credibilidad.
teaching.explanationEs: Autoría, datos y método son los tres primeros filtros para valorar una fuente.
segments: Before relying on a source, a critical reader asks who wrote it and what data
it offers, because a source with no author and no evidence has little credibility.
teaching.audioText: Before relying on a source, a critical reader asks who wrote it and what data it offers, because a source with no author and no evidence has little credibility.

teaching.en: A cautious reader treats anecdotal evidence, a single story told with conviction, as suggestive rather than reliable, and says so with may or seems.
teaching.es: Un lector cauto trata la evidencia anecdótica, una sola historia contada con convicción, como sugerente y no como fiable, y lo expresa con may o seems.
teaching.explanationEs: May, seems y tend to son señales de cautela; su ausencia suele indicar exageración.
segments: A cautious reader treats anecdotal evidence, a single story told with conviction,
as suggestive rather than reliable, and says so with may or seems.
teaching.audioText: A cautious reader treats anecdotal evidence, a single story told with conviction, as suggestive rather than reliable, and says so with may or seems.

teaching.en: Fluency is not perfection: a confident speaker disagrees with tact, asks I was wondering whether you had considered this, and keeps going after a slip.
teaching.es: La fluidez no es perfección: quien habla con seguridad discrepa con tacto, pregunta «me preguntaba si habías considerado esto» y sigue adelante tras un desliz.
teaching.explanationEs: La pregunta indirecta con whether suena a duda razonable, no a acusación.
segments: Fluency is not perfection: a confident speaker disagrees with tact, asks I was
wondering whether you had considered this, and keeps going after a slip.
teaching.audioText: Fluency is not perfection: a confident speaker disagrees with tact, asks I was wondering whether you had considered this, and keeps going after a slip.

teaching.en: A documented revision closes the task convincingly and leaves the reader confident that you control your own text: I wrote less people, then changed it to fewer people.
teaching.es: Una revisión documentada cierra la tarea de forma convincente y deja al lector seguro de que controlas tu propio texto: escribí less people y lo cambié por fewer people.
teaching.explanationEs: Documentar una revisión (I changed…, or rather…) muestra qué cambiaste y por qué.
segments: A documented revision closes the task convincingly and leaves the reader confident that you
control your own text: I wrote less people, then changed it to fewer people.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase cuenta un antecedente personal con tiempos coherentes?

choices.text: Years ago, I use to dread meetings in English; by the time I joined the club, I had already stopped rehearsing every sentence.
Years ago, I used to dread meetings in English; by the time I joined the club, I had already stopped rehearsing every sentence.
Years ago, I used to dread meetings in English; by the time I joined the club, I have already stopped rehearsing every sentence.

feedback.es: Used to + verbo base describe el estado pasado y had already stopped sitúa el cambio antes de otro hecho pasado; las demás mezclan formas.

hint.es: Fíjate en used to + verbo base y en el tiempo de lo que ocurrió antes de otro hecho pasado.

prompt.es: Completa: «Por eso, sus conclusiones quizá no sean fiables.»

feedback.es: Una muestra mínima y sesgada resta fiabilidad: el adjetivo que encaja con may not be es reliable.

hint.es: Adjetivo que describe una fuente en la que se puede confiar.

origin.text: The survey was answered by only twelve people, all of them friends of the author. For that reason, its conclusions may not be ___.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Me preguntaba si habías considerado la otra postura.»

answer.text: I was wondering whether you had considered the other view

feedback.es: La pregunta indirecta con whether mantiene el orden afirmativo: whether you had considered.

hint.es: Empieza con la fórmula de petición indirecta; el sujeto va antes del verbo.

prompt.es: ¿Cómo valora con cautela esta fuente una lectora crítica?

choices.text: Surprising enough that it deserves to be taken seriously.
Bold but anecdotal, so it deserves little credibility.
Plausible, so the missing figures hardly matter.
False, because its author prefers not to give a name.

feedback.es: Una afirmación rotunda sin cifras y apoyada en un caso personal es anecdótica; la prudencia pide dudar, no declararla falsa.

origin.text: A post by an unnamed user claims that nine out of ten learners who study at night fail their exams, and adds that colleges have been hiding the truth. No figures are given, and the only evidence is the writer's own cousin.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cómo reacciona la hablante ante una postura contraria.

choices.text: She disagrees politely and keeps the discussion open.
She drops her objection out of respect for the other view.
She insists that any further discussion would be a waste of time.

feedback.es: Concede el respeto, mantiene su postura con «I would argue» y propone algo con «I was wondering whether»: desacuerdo con tacto.

origin.audio: Much as I respect your view, I would argue that the plan needs more time. I was wondering whether we could ask the students first. I would not want to ignore what you have seen, though; perhaps we could look at both.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase del caso final con la hebra del programa que demuestra.

pairs: Years ago, I used to live in a small town
Much as I dislike the cost, I would argue it is worth it
The source may not be reliable
I was wondering whether we could discuss it
I wrote less people, but I changed it to fewer

feedback.es: Cada frase pone en juego una de las cinco hebras: relato, argumento, cautela, tacto y revisión.

prompt.es: ¿Qué implica el autor sobre quienes dan por muerta la carta en papel?

choices.text: They are quite right that the paper letter has now lost all of its worth for us.
They are right that letters are disappearing but wrong to regret the loss.
They should stop writing letters and use a keyboard instead.
They mix up the end of a format with the end of a way of thinking.

feedback.es: El autor concede lo del sobre y sugiere que lo que se pierde no es el papel, sino el modo de pensar que obliga a decidir qué importa.

origin.text: Commentators like to announce that the paper letter has disappeared. They may be right about the envelope, but I doubt that they are right about the habit. A letter makes a writer decide what matters before a single word is written, and that way of thinking, rather than the paper, is what we should be sorry to lose.

prompt.es: ¿Qué versión ajusta la frase sin cambiar su grado de certeza?

choices.text: If the survey proves unreliable, the committee will probably reject its conclusions.
If the survey proves unreliable, the committee will certainly reject its conclusions.
If the survey proves unreliable, the committee may consider its conclusions.
The committee will reject the survey's conclusions because it is unreliable.

feedback.es: Probably conserva la cautela de most likely; certainly la elimina y las otras dos cambian la condición o el sentido.

origin.text: In the event that the survey should be found to be unreliable, the committee will, most likely, be in a position to reject its conclusions.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige la valoración más acertada de esta charla.

choices.text: Weak in evidence and tact: one anecdote and rude words for critics.
Weak in structure, yet respectful and well supported by a lot of data.
Strong in tact, since it concedes several important points to its critics.

feedback.es: Solo aporta el caso de un amigo y llama absurda a la postura contraria: fallan la evidencia y el tacto.

origin.audio: Good evening. I want to talk about remote work. Everyone knows that it is better, so there is really nothing to discuss. My friend works from home and has never been happier. Some people say that offices build teams, but that is complete nonsense. Anyway, I also wanted to mention my holiday in Cuenca, which was wonderful. To finish, companies that refuse remote work will lose their best staff, and they deserve to. Finally, I should say that I have never understood why anybody would choose a daily commute, and I doubt that anyone who tried working from home would ever go back.

prompt.es: Caso final: responde con las cinco hebras del programa (260–320 palabras).

answer.text: Years ago, I used to believe that I would never speak English well. I had never spoken with a stranger in English, and I was afraid of making mistakes. Then I started studying with an app every morning, and in hindsight that routine was the start of my journey. The article says that students who learn with apps never speak fluently. Admittedly, an app alone may not be enough: it cannot give you a real conversation. Much as I respect the author, I would argue that the claim is too strong. The source seems to rely on a small survey, and its evidence looks anecdotal, so its conclusion may not be reliable. I was wondering whether the author could explain how many students took part. I understand that a short article has little space, and I appreciate the concern about speaking well. Revision: I first wrote that apps are useless for speaking, or rather, I should say that they are useful but not enough. On balance, the best plan is an app plus real conversations, and that is exactly what this course has given me, so I feel confident now.
accepted: Years ago, I used to believe that I would never speak English well. I had never spoken with a stranger in English, and I was afraid of making mistakes. Then I started studying with an app every morning, and in hindsight that routine was the start of my journey. The article says that students who learn with apps never speak fluently. Admittedly, an app alone may not be enough: it cannot give you a real conversation. Much as I respect the author, I would argue that the claim is too strong. The source seems to rely on a small survey, and its evidence looks anecdotal, so its conclusion may not be reliable. I was wondering whether the author could explain how many students took part. I understand that a short article has little space, and I appreciate the concern about speaking well. Revision: I first wrote that apps are useless for speaking, or rather, I should say that they are useful but not enough. On balance, the best plan is an app plus real conversations, and that is exactly what this course has given me, so I feel confident now.

When I was a child, I would watch films in English without understanding a word, and my cousin used to laugh at me. Later, I had to take an exam, and that was the moment when I decided to learn properly. An online post claims that apps are a waste of time and that nobody learns to speak with them. It is true that an app cannot replace a teacher. Even though I agree with part of that view, I think the post may be wrong, because it gives no numbers and does not say who wrote it. The source seems weak, so I would be careful before believing it. I was wondering whether the author has ever used an app for a full year. With respect, one experience does not prove a rule. I appreciate that some people learn better with a teacher, and I see your point. Let me rephrase my conclusion: apps do not teach everything, but they help you to start. In the end, I changed my opinion only a little, and this course helped me to explain why.

feedback.es: El caso final integra antecedente, argumento con concesión, evaluación cautelosa de la fuente, tacto y una revisión documentada.

origin.text: Un artículo afirma: «Los estudiantes que aprenden inglés con apps nunca llegan a hablar con fluidez.» Responde: cuenta un antecedente personal con tiempos coherentes; argumenta con concesión y refutación matizada; evalúa la fuente con cautela; muestra tacto ante quien piensa distinto; y termina documentando una revisión (or rather…).

prompt.es: ¿Qué demuestra la autora con esta nota final sobre su borrador?

choices.text: That she regrets having taken the course at all.
That she wants her reader to rewrite the sentence.
That she can document a revision and justify it.
That she has lost confidence in her own writing.

feedback.es: Dice qué escribió, por qué era un error y qué cambió: es una revisión documentada, no un arrepentimiento.

origin.text: My first draft said that the course was easy. On reflection, that was careless: it was demanding, but it never felt impossible. I have therefore changed the sentence and added an example of a week when I nearly gave up.

prompt.es: Completa: «Al mirar atrás, cada pequeño paso importó más de lo que parecía.»

feedback.es: Look back on es la colocación para repasar el pasado con perspectiva; la preposición on introduce lo recordado.

origin.text: Looking ___ on the whole journey, I can see that every small step mattered more than it seemed at the time.

prompt.es: Cierra tu último mensaje con una frase de confianza sobre tu recorrido.

answer.text: In hindsight, it has been a long journey, but I feel confident that I can use English with fluency and tact.
accepted: In hindsight, it has been a long journey, but I feel confident that I can use English with fluency and tact.
Looking back, I am proud of my journey, and I feel confident that my fluency has grown.
Looking back, this course was a real milestone, and I am confident that my fluency will keep growing.

feedback.es: Una frase de cierre con hindsight, journey y confident resume tu progreso con perspectiva y seguridad.

origin.text: Has terminado el curso de inglés. Escribe una frase final que muestre que te sientes seguro, que miras atrás con perspectiva y que valoras tu fluidez.
